findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user who has never interacted with the topic has no topic_users row). The code then unconditionally calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!`, raising NoMethodError on nil and returning a 500. The unsubscribe link is sent in notification emails to any notified user, including users who never opened the topic, so this path is reachable in production. The code should use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` (which creates the row if missing, as done in #set_notifications) or guard for nil.

findings.title: unsubscribe action does not verify the user can see the topic
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe builds `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` but never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!` on the topic. TopicView.new may not raise for topics in restricted categories the user cannot access (unlike #show, which rescues Discourse::InvalidAccess). The action then mutates the user's TopicUser notification level and calls perform_show_response, which serializes the topic view — potentially leaking topic existence/content (title, excerpt via @description_meta) for topics in secure categories to unauthorized logged-in users. Compare with #toggle_mute and #clear_pin which call `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic)`.

findings.title: unsubscribe toggles notification level instead of unsubscribing, and mutates state on a GET request
findings.body: The unsubscribe endpoint is a GET route (config/routes.rb lines 440-441) that permanently mutates the user's TopicUser notification_level (a side effect on GET, which breaks web semantics, makes the link prefetchable/crawlable, and means email scanners or browser prefetchers silently change user state). Worse, the toggle logic is wrong for an 'unsubscribe' action: if the user is watching/tracking (level > regular) it sets level to regular — i.e. clicking 'stop receiving notifications about this topic' leaves the user at 'regular', which still sends emails for this topic. The intent (per the email copy 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic') is to set the level to muted. The else-branch muting only happens when the user is already at regular or muted, so a watching user who clicks unsubscribe keeps receiving notifications.

findings.title: unsubscribe renders the full topic show response, leaking topic content and tracking a visit
findings.body: After mutating notification state, #unsubscribe calls perform_show_response, which renders the full topics/show template with the preloaded TopicViewSerializer (all posts the user can see, topic metadata) and sets @description_meta from the topic excerpt. The Ember route (topic-unsubscribe.js.es6) only needs the topic's id/title/notification state, not the entire topic payload. This both leaks more data than the unsubscribe page needs and is wasteful. It also means the unsubscribe URL behaves like a topic view (canonical URL, meta description), which is incorrect for a state-changing endpoint.

findings.title: Unsubscribe route fetches the full topic view instead of the lightweight unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The route's model hook calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which loads the entire topic (all posts) — the same heavy request as viewing the topic — even though the server-side unsubscribe action (TopicsController#unsubscribe) already performs the state change when the URL is hit. The Ember route is registered at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, but the browser first hits the Rails route (GET topics#unsubscribe) which mutates state and renders the show template with preloaded data; the Ember app then re-fetches the full topic view client-side. This doubles the work and loads the whole post stream just to display a one-line confirmation page. The route should rely on the preloaded topic data from the server render (like topic-from-params does via modelFor) or fetch a minimal topic payload.

findings.title: Typo in property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing 'i' in 'Notifications'), and the template references `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` so it works, but the misspelling will confuse future maintainers and any external references. Rename to `stopNotificationsText` in both the controller and the template.

findings.title: Triple-stache rendering of stopNotificiationsText injects the topic title as raw HTML
findings.body: The template renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (unescaped). The controller builds this string via `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, and the locale string is "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}." — the tags require unescaped output, but so does the interpolated topic title. `fancyTitle` is HTML-escaped server-side (Topic#fancy_title calls ERB::Util.html_escape), but I18n interpolation in the JS client does not re-escape, and any markup that survives in fancyTitle (e.g. entities produced by SmartyPants rendering, or double-encoding edge cases) is injected raw into the DOM. This is an XSS risk if fancyTitle ever contains unescaped content (e.g. via plugins or serializer changes). Safer: keep the in the template and interpolate the title with escaped {{ }}, e.g. `You will stop receiving notifications for {{model.fancyTitle}}.` in the template itself.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url passed to email template args is never defined for digest and other non-notification emails
findings.body: send_notification_email now always passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` into email_opts, and the locale string `unsubscribe_link` (server.en.yml) now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Email::MessageBuilder#body and #html_part call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. Any email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true but without an unsubscribe_url opt (e.g. the digest mailer, which sets add_unsubscribe_link via build_email defaults — check digest path in user_notifications.rb which does not go through send_notification_email) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when rendering the unsubscribe link. The digest email (UserNotifications#digest) does not pass unsubscribe_url, so digest emails with the unsubscribe footer will fail to build/send.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header still points only to user preferences, not the per-topic unsubscribe URL
findings.body: header_args sets `result['List-Unsubscribe'] = "<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>"` when add_unsubscribe_link is set. The PR adds a per-topic unsubscribe_url to template_args, but the List-Unsubscribe header (the machine-readable one-click unsubscribe used by Gmail etc.) still points to the generic preferences page. For one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058 / Gmail's unsubscribe button) to actually stop topic notifications, the header should use the per-topic unsubscribe_url when present: `result['List-Unsubscribe'] = "<#{template_args[:unsubscribe_url] || template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>"`. As written, mail clients offering 'unsubscribe' will send users to preferences instead of stopping topic emails, and the feature is only half-wired.

findings.title: respond_instructions placeholder emitted inside the context-posts block
findings.body:
The template renders `
%{respond_instructions}
` both inside the `if context_posts.present?` block (line 6) and again unconditionally at line 19. When context posts exist, the respond instructions appear twice in the HTML email. The first occurrence (inside the context block, before the 'previous discussion' posts) appears to be a leftover from the re-indentation; it should be removed so instructions appear only once at the bottom.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link locale text says 'these emails' for the per-topic link
findings.body: The first sentence of the expanded unsubscribe_link text reads 'To unsubscribe from these emails, visit your [user preferences](%{user_preferences_url}).' followed by 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).' The first sentence is now inaccurate/misleading in notification emails: the preferences link unsubscribes from all notification emails, not 'these emails' (the topic-specific ones). Reword to e.g. 'To unsubscribe from all emails, visit your [user preferences](...).' so users don't think the preferences link only affects the current topic's emails.

findings.title: afterModel sets a nested property path that Ember.set may not observe correctly
findings.body: `topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)` sets a nested path on the topic model. In this Ember version, setting a nested path via a single set() call works, but the topic's `details` object comes from updateFromJson and may be a plain object; also the intent (per the comment 'hide the notification reason text') is to suppress the notification banner on this page. If `details` is undefined at that point (updateFromJson may not have created it), set() will throw or silently fail. Safer to guard: `if (topic.get('details')) { topic.set('details.notificationReasonText', null); }` or set the whole details object. Without a test this is unverified behavior.

findings.title: No test verifies the per-topic unsubscribe_url appears in the email body or List-Unsubscribe header
findings.body: The spec adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the message_with_unsubscribe builder, but the assertions only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains the user_preferences_url. Nothing asserts that the body contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL (the new locale string interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}), nor that the header uses it. Given the mailer change and the locale change, a regression that drops unsubscribe_url from template_args (raising I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument) or renders the wrong link would not be caught. Add assertions that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` includes '/t/1234/unsubscribe' and that the rendered unsubscribe_link text contains it.

findings.title: unsubscribe added to skip_before_filter :check_xhr, allowing non-XHR state changes
findings.body: The PR adds :unsubscribe to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. check_xhr exists to reject non-XHR requests to JSON API endpoints; skipping it for unsubscribe means the endpoint accepts plain browser GETs (which is required for email links, so this is intentional), but it also means the action must handle HTML and JSON formats itself — which it does via perform_show_response's respond_to. This is acceptable for an email-link endpoint, but note the action is also now reachable via direct navigation and will render the full topic page HTML; combined with the missing guardian check (separate finding) this widens exposure. No code change strictly required, but the security review of the HTML path should be deliberate.

findings.title: dropdown-button title is concatenated into HTML without escaping
findings.body:
renderString now conditionally pushes `"

" + title + "

"` where title comes from `this.get('title')`. Previously the title was always rendered (same injection), so this is not a regression, but the value is interpolated raw into an HTML string buffer. If any caller passes a user-controlled title (e.g. a topic title), this is an XSS vector. The surrounding code also interpolates row.title, row.description, and id unescaped (lines 44-47), so the component generally assumes trusted input. Worth noting as a latent XSS risk, especially since the new unsubscribe page embeds this component via topic-notifications-button.
